documents.abstract: Introduction. Despite the active integration of large language models into education, systemic patterns, comparative effectiveness of prompt engineering integration levels, and sustainability of effects remain understudied. The aim of this research is to identify patterns of prompt engineering influence on educational project management, to conduct a comparative assessment of the instrumental, processual, and cognitive levels of integration, and to reveal the factors ensuring the sustainability of the obtained results. Materials and Methods. The research methodology was built on a three-component framework. Theoretical analysis set the frame for the action research, which involved 117 master’s students divided into control and experimental groups. The statistical block included correlation and regression analysis, ANOVA with Tukey’s post-hoc criterion, Student's t-test, and η² calculation. Qualitative shifts were assessed through content analysis of reflective reports–this made it possible to track not only quantitative but also meaningful changes. Measurements were taken three times: before the experiment began, immediately upon completion of the project cycle, and three months later. Results. The empirical data made it possible to identify three stable patterns. A direct relationship was found between the development of prompt competencies and the completeness of project risk identification (r = 0,73; p < 0,01). At the same time, the dynamics of efficiency turned out to be non-linear. The greatest increase occurs in the range of 45–60 prompts per project, while exceeding this threshold leads to a decline in marginal returns (R² = 0,68; p < 0,01). The functional role of prompts changes depending on the phase of the project life cycle: correlation coefficients range from 0.52 to 0.71, indicating that no single prompt solution exists for all stages. The contribution of integration levels to the total variance is hierarchically structured: the cognitive level accounts for 33% (η² = 0,33), the procedural level for 29% (η² = 0,29), and the instrumental level for 14% (η² = 0,14). All intergroup differences are statistically significant (p < 0,001). The stability of the achieved effects differs quite sharply between the groups. Three months after the withdrawal of AI support, the experimental group retained 89,5% of the indicators, while the control group retained only 65,4% (p < 0,001). Factors ensuring this stability include the following: the institutionalization of template solutions, participants’ reflexive practices, and a verification system based on the ‘human-in-the-loop’ model. According to the data, these are the factors that function as predictors of long-term effect. Conclusions. The data obtained enabled to make three proposals that hold the status of scientific generalizations–concerning the identified patterns of prompt engineering integration, the established hierarchy of its structural components, and the mechanisms for sustaining effects over time. Prompt engineering, in the proposed interpretation, is qualified as a multi-level system comprising instrumental, organizational, and cognitive strata, which fundamentally distinguishes the presented concept from approaches developed in prior works. These theoretical constructs and empirical data provide a foundation for further research in the field of human-machine interaction in the field of educational design.

The integration of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) into higher education has outpaced the development of pedagogical models capable of directing it towards higher-order learning. Unstructured, zero-shot interaction with Large Language Models tends to yield fluent but uncritical output, while conventional assessment instruments are not designed to capture the quality of a learner's interaction with an AI system. This article addresses that gap by presenting the design of a Personalized Multi-Agent System (MAS) built upon the CIDI (Clarify, Ideate, Develop, Implement) pedagogical framework, together with the assessment architecture required to evaluate it. Following a design-based research methodology, four components are specified. First, the CIDI framework is articulated as a four-stage model of structured human-AI interaction, grounded in Distributed Cognition Theory and Cognitive Load Theory. Second, a dual-agent architecture is specified in full: an Ideation Agent configured for divergent generation and a Critical Evaluator Agent configured for convergent methodological critique, each defined by its system prompt and temperature configuration, and both integrated into an institutional Learning Management System. Third, a complete instructional design is presented, implementing the framework as a four-stage research-planning task within a research methodology curriculum, and introducing the Iterative Refinement Cycle (IRC) as an observable indicator of dialogic engagement recoverable from LMS logs. Fourth, two purpose-built assessment instruments are introduced: a 100-point Cognitive Competence Score rubric addressing problem formulation, methodological rigour, logical structuring and academic literacy; and an analytic rubric operationalizing Torrance's four dimensions of divergent thinking. The article concludes with a validation protocol specifying the design, reliability indices and analytic procedures required for subsequent empirical testing. The contribution is methodological: it supplies a reproducible architecture and a transparent instrumentation set for research on structured human-AI interaction in higher education.

documents.abstract: Abstract The rapid advancement of generative artificial intelligence is transforming marketing communication, with AI-generated voices emerging as an increasingly important means through which brands communicate with consumers. This paper examines AI-generated voices from a consumer psychology perspective, focusing on how consumers interpret and respond to synthetic voices used in marketing communication. Drawing on literature from artificial intelligence, marketing, consumer behaviour and human–computer interaction, the paper explores the psychological significance of vocal characteristics such as naturalness, human-likeness, prosody, anthropomorphism and emotional expression. It further examines how these characteristics can shape consumer perceptions of message credibility, authenticity and brand trust. The discussion highlights the growing use of AI-generated voices across advertising, social media, voice commerce and interactive brand communication, with selected examples from the Indian marketing context illustrating their applications in personalisation, engagement and localisation. The paper argues that the effectiveness of AI-generated voices depends not simply on technological sophistication, but on how consumers psychologically interpret the voice and its relationship with the message and brand. The paper concludes by identifying directions for future research on AI-mediated brand communication.

Contemporary therapeutic, contemplative, and cognitive practices use partially overlapping vocabularies for internal constraint, awareness, participation, and change. This paper asks whether four constructs developed elsewhere in the Ableman corpus--the Ableman Prime Directive (APD), Epistemic Situational Awareness (ESA), Ableman Consciousness Ontology (ACO), and Terminability--can function as a common comparison grammar across those practices. The proposal separates four questions: whether an internal binding is detectable, refusable, and renegotiable; whether a cognitive operation is self-locating and knows when continuation has lost warrant; what grade of meaning-binding participation is available in a given state; and what weight attaches to preserving or ending a temporally extended internal thread. The variables are intentionally non-substitutable. A gain on one axis does not establish a gain on another, and no scalar score is proposed. The paper's cross-modality mappings are hypotheses for conceptual analysis and empirical study, not findings about clinical efficacy, diagnostic categories, or treatment selection. The framework does not replace clinical judgment, modality-specific training, safety practice, or evidence-based care. Its immediate contribution is narrower: a typed vocabulary for stating what a practice may be changing, where two practices may differ, and what evidence would be required before using the map clinically. The result is a research program as much as a framework. It specifies a formal core, a candidate modality map, failure modes, a realization funnel from conceptual specification to evidence and revision, and clear boundaries between corpus-derived architecture and claims that require external clinical validation.

documents.abstract: Analyst burnout in security operations centers is not mainly a volume problem. It is a structure problem. Logs from endpoints, cloud services, and network devices sit in one tool, while the threat intelligence that would make sense of those logs sits in five or six others. An analyst chasing a suspicious IP typically opens Virus Total, OTX, and a few OSINT feeds manually before getting an answer, and that workflow breaks quickly when the queue has twenty open cases. ThreatFusion AI addresses this at the architecture level. We built a temporal knowledge graph that holds internal telemetry, open-source threat feeds, and MITRE ATT&CK technique mappings in one queryable structure. A team of specialized LLM agents works against that graph to check whether an indicator or behavior pattern has appeared before and which campaign it might belong to. Before any automated containment step executes, a dedicated guardrail agent validates it against policy rules. Low-risk steps go through SOAR automatically; anything higher-impact waits for a human analyst. This paper describes the six-layer architecture, the reasoning behind each design decision, and the evaluation methodology we are running against simulated attack traffic.

The classification of Hindi-English (Hinglish) code-mixed hate speech (HS) is greatly affected by the spread of fake news on social media. However, key challenges include the need for high-quality annotated code-mixed data and difficulties in handling evolving slang and cultural expressions. This work introduces ToxiFusionNet, a transformer-based model that can detect and analyse toxic, fake and hateful Hindi-English code-mixed posts on social media. Data were collected from online sources using application programming interfaces (APIs) and web-scraping tools. The data were then examined for duplicate or near-duplicate posts. Subsequently, to normalize Hinglish code-mixed content, the pipeline removes emojis, performs transliteration and translation, eliminates stop words, tokenizes the text, and applies stemming. The annotation process comprised two stages: first, determining whether the content was fake or hateful; and second, grouping the content according to the target (religion, caste, region, gender and cyberbullying) and the severity of hate (low, medium, high). The ToxiFusionNet integrates part-of-speech (POS) tags, sentiment scores, word-to-vector (Word2Vec) embeddings and Toxic Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (ToxicBERT) derived indicators to combine linguistic, semantic, and toxicity-related information. Its multi-task architecture incorporates task-specific loss functions, layer pruning, dropout, batch normalization, and explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) techniques to support model interpretation. On the internal test set, the framework achieved an accuracy of 0.980 for fake/non-fake classification and an F1-score of 0.978 for fake class. For hate/non-hate detection, it achieved a weighted F1-score of 0.975. The reported accuracy of 0.980 represents an improvement of 2.2 percentage points over HateBERT (0.958), confirming its effectiveness in detecting complex code-mixed HS. External evaluation on the HASOC 2021 dataset yielded an accuracy of 0.968 and F1-csore of 0.965. Human evaluation of token-level explanations yielded Cohen’s kappa values of 0.76, 0.79, and 0.81 for integrated gradients (IG), SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), local interpretable model-agnostic explanations (LIME) respectively. These results suggest that ToxiFusionNet may support the identification and prioritization of potentially harmful code-mixed content for human review. Its suitability for near-real-time deployment requires further validation under operational under conditions.

Abstract Background The applications of artificial intelligence (AI) in nursing encompass a wide array of domains, including nursing practice, management, and education. Considering that nurses serve as the core group on the frontline of healthcare, their attitudes toward AI may be crucial for promoting the rational development of AI in the nursing field. However, there is currently no validated instrument available in China to assess nurses’ attitudes toward AI. This study aimed to translate the Artificial Intelligence Attitude Scale for Nurses (AIASN) and evaluate its psychometric properties among Chinese nurses. Methods This methodological study enrolled a sample consisting of 1309 nurses. The Chinese translation of the AIASN was generated using a commonly used instrument validation guideline. The validity of the instrument was assessed using content validity, structural validity (including Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA), Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA), and Exploratory Structural Equation Modeling (ESEM)), convergent validity, and discriminant validity. The reliability of the instrument was assessed using internal consistency reliability and test-retest reliability. Results A five-factor model was obtained through EFA. This model showed satisfactory model fit in CFA and ESEM (CFI = 0.955, TLI = 0.926, RMSEA = 0.068, SRMR = 0.023). The Cronbach’s α coefficient for the instrument was 0.906. The intraclass correlation coefficient for the instrument was 0.819. Conclusions The Chinese version of the AIASN comprises five dimensions and 25 items, demonstrating robust psychometric properties for assessing Chinese nurses’ attitudes toward AI. It can help nursing educators develop AI-related education and training programs and identify nurses’ learning needs.

documents.abstract: Assessment in Arabic language learning as a foreign language (Arabic as a Foreign Language) is currently undergoing a significant paradigm shift. This transformation is influenced by the development of digital technology, the utilization of Artificial Intelligence (AI), and the implementation of the Merdeka Curriculum in Indonesia, which emphasizes flexibility, differentiation, and learning personalization. This article presents a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) aimed at identifying, examining, and synthesizing developments, innovations, methodological approaches, and various challenges in the assessment of the four Arabic language skills, namely listening, speaking, reading, and writing, during the period from 2020 to early 2026. The review employed the PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) protocol to identify and analyze relevant literature. The findings indicate a shift from conventional evaluation systems based on discrete tests toward the implementation of Technology-Enhanced Assessment (TEA) and more authentic forms of assessment. The literature synthesis reveals several key findings. First, diagnostic assessment, encompassing both cognitive and non-cognitive aspects, plays an important role in designing differentiated learning within the framework of the Merdeka Curriculum. Second, the development of assessment instruments for Arabic language maharah is increasingly oriented toward measuring higher-order thinking skills (Higher Order Thinking Skills/HOTS). Third, the utilization of Generative AI, including ChatGPT, as well as various gamification-based learning platforms, has introduced new approaches to providing faster, more adaptive, and interactive feedback. Based on the synthesis, the effectiveness of modern assessment is not determined solely by the sophistication of the technology employed, but also by the alignment between technology and pedagogical objectives, the transparency of assessment procedures, and its ability to comprehensively represent learners' communicative competence while maintaining the principles of academic integrity.

documents.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly reshaping the structure and pedagogy of contemporary education systems. This study examines Türkiye’s strategic vision and institutional orientations toward AI in education by analyzing official policy documents and mapping their theoretical foundations within a structured conceptual framework. This study employed a qualitative document analysis design, examining 14 policy documents, strategic plans, ethical guidelines, and curriculum documents published by the Presidency of the Republic of Türkiye, the Ministry of National Education, the Council of Higher Education, and TÜBİTAK between 2021 and 2029. The data were analyzed using thematic content analysis, and the documents were thematically coded using NVivo. The findings indicate that official education policy documents frame AI as a multidimensional paradigm shaped by institutional priorities. AI integration is presented as a predominantly top-down process, with official documents emphasizing advanced engineering applications for secondary education and gifted students, while AI applications for preschool and primary education receive comparatively less attention. AI is portrayed as a tool that supports instructional design while reducing teachers’ administrative and academic workload. At the same time, the ‘human-in-the-loop’ principle is identified as a core safeguard within the national policy framework. The analysis also reveals a restrictive approach to the use of AI in academic assessment. Based on these findings, the study proposes several policy recommendations. These include integrating age-appropriate AI activities into primary education curricula, establishing standardized data anonymization principles to protect student information, and redesigning pre-service and in-service teacher education through practice-oriented professional development aligned with teachers’ evolving roles.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Medical large language models (LLMs) achieving high benchmark accuracy exhibit unexplained variability in clinical tasks, producing errors that clinicians cannot safeguard against. We evaluated clinical reasoning stability in GPT-5, MedGemma-27B-Text-IT, and OpenBioLLM-Llama3-70B using 355 systematic perturbations of physician-validated oncology cases and trained sparse autoencoders on 1 billion tokens from 50,000 MIMIC-IV clinical notes to decompose their internal representation. We find models exhibit dramatic reasoning instability, shifting staging accuracy by over 50% based solely on prompt format, or generating definitive staging in clinically insufficient scenarios. Sparse autoencoder analysis revealed hierarchical encoding in MedGemma, where high-magnitude features encode lexical identity and low-magnitude features encode contextual meaning. OpenBioLLM distributes information uniformly. We demonstrate these internal encoding structures differentially affect retrieval interventions, suggesting interventions effective for one architecture may harm another. We recommend healthcare institutions implement architecture-specific safety validation, as benchmark equivalence does not imply functional equivalence, with implications for AI safety beyond healthcare.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: The wardrobe, as a fundamental component of domestic space, mediates the daily ritual of clothing selection, storage, and self-presentation, yet its design has historically been driven by manufacturing conventions rather than systematic engagement with user needs. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, this systematic review conducted a comprehensive literature search across Scopus and Web of Science. After strict screening based on inclusion and exclusion criteria, 68 high-quality studies were finally included for systematic coding and thematic synthesis. Thematic synthesis yielded seven interconnected themes: user needs and requirements, ergonomic design, cognitive and behavioral dimensions, smart and intelligent wardrobes, customization and modular systems, accessibility and inclusive design, and cultural and aesthetic considerations. Findings reveal that UCD methods can substantially improve wardrobe usability, accessibility, and user satisfaction, yet the literature remains fragmented across disciplinary silos, methodologically constrained by short-duration laboratory studies. Three critical research gaps are identified: the absence of longitudinal field studies, insufficient participant diversity, limited real-world validation of smart wardrobe prototypes, poor integration across thematic domains, and neglect of sustainability as a design dimension. The review concludes by articulating a forward-looking research agenda and practical guidance for designers, manufacturers, and educators seeking to place the user at the center of wardrobe design.

In recent years, the intersection of artificial intelligence (AI) and creative writing has opened new possibilities in producing educational content. This paper explores the process of co-authoring a children's book on astronomy using AI as a writing assistant, under the supervision of a subject matter expert. While AI has advanced significantly in generating coherent, relevant text, human guidance is crucial to ensure scientific accuracy, pedagogical appropriateness, and an engaging narrative tailored to young readers. In this case study, I, the principal author and co-creator, utilized AI writing tools to draft a book aimed at children aged 7 to 14, explaining key astronomical concepts in an accessible and engaging way. The book, titled “Los Fundamentos de la Astronomia" was framed within the context of Colombia's night sky, making it both regionally relevant and scientifically sound. The project originated from my attendance at an astronomy conference in Athens, Greece, where I met José, a Colombian astronomer who described the challenges of teaching astronomy in Colombia using textbooks written from a European perspective. The positional differences in celestial observations between Spain and Colombia created significant confusion for his students. Recognizing an opportunity to address this regional educational gap, I proposed a collaboration using AI as a tool combined with his astronomical expertise to create culturally appropriate educational materials. Keywords: Collaboration between AI, the Astronomer, and the Co-Author
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Strategic environments are increasingly characterized by uncertainty, rapid technological change, and disruptions that may initially appear as low-visibility or ambiguous signals. Existing approaches to weak-signal analysis, strategic foresight, early-warning systems, and artificial intelligence address parts of this challenge but remain fragmented, particularly in connecting signal detection with interpretation and strategic assessment. This study develops Weak-Signal Intelligence (WSI) as an AI-enabled organizational capability for detecting, interpreting, integrating, and evaluating weak signals to anticipate emerging strategic disruptions. Using a conceptual theory-building and intelligent modeling approach, the study integrates insights from weak-signal research, strategic foresight, early-warning systems, artificial intelligence, sensemaking, uncertainty, and complexity. The proposed framework connects signal detection, interpretation, pattern recognition, uncertainty analytics, disruption assessment, strategic response intelligence, and adaptive learning. The model positions WSI as a continuous human–AI process that transforms low-visibility signals into uncertainty-aware strategic early-warning intelligence. The study contributes a conceptual foundation for improving strategic awareness and preparedness and provides directions for future empirical validation, measurement development, and cross-sector application.

Web-based and mobile artificial intelligence tools have spread rapidly in Southeast Asian universities, yet evidence on what they achieved in real learning remained fragmented. This systematic review synthesised empirical studies that implemented or evaluated such tools in degree-level higher education in Southeast Asia between 2021 and 2026. Following the PRISMA 2020 guideline, 642 Scopus records were screened, 79 full texts were assessed and 59 studies were included. Study quality was appraised with the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool, measured outcomes were summarised by effect direction, and findings were integrated through three-stage thematic synthesis. Most studies came from Indonesia, Vietnam and Thailand, concerned language learning, used general-purpose chatbots and relied on non-randomised designs. Of 45 studies that measured learning, 36 reported improvements, mainly in uncontrolled designs or against routine teaching, whereas four of six comparisons with equivalent human support found no difference. Five analytical themes emerged: polished products with uncertain learning, pedagogy over presence, an affective double edge, unequal readiness and comparator-dependent conclusions. The evidence supported these tools as comparable and scalable complements within teacher-mediated, bounded designs rather than as superior replacements. The review proposed an orchestration framework and a research agenda that prioritised active comparators and independent, delayed measures of learning.
topics: Intelligent Tutoring Systems and Adaptive Learning
Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Purpose This paper examines how cognition operates under conditions of prolonged organizational strain where demands persist, interpretations do not converge and disengagement does not occur. It challenges the dominant assumption in organizational behavior that cognitive processes under strain are inherently directional and oriented toward resolution, coherence or withdrawal. Design/methodology/approach The paper develops a conceptual framework through integrative analysis of stress and coping, sensemaking and burnout literatures. It identifies a shared directional assumption across these perspectives and demonstrates its limitations under conditions of sustained and indeterminate strain. A new construct is introduced and formalized through a set of theoretical propositions. Findings The analysis shows that individuals may sustain cognitive engagement without reducing demands, achieving interpretive coherence or disengaging. To account for this pattern, the paper introduces cognitive flexibility under prolonged organizational strain, defined as a mode of functioning characterized by interpretive openness, non-directional engagement and ongoing meaning adjustment without convergence. Originality/value The paper contributes by identifying prolonged organizational strain as a distinct condition and re-specifying adaptation as sustained cognitive functioning without directional progression. It extends organizational behavior theory by explaining how cognition operates when resolution, coherence and disengagement do not structure activity.

Artificial intelligence (AI) is turning dynamic pricing from a standardized management decision into an individual, algorithmic experience. Algorithmic pricing improves efficiency and personalization, but its opacity and individualized prices can leave consumers feeling treated unfairly and distrustful. This short communication draws on recent research on algorithmic pricing, price fairness, price transparency, and consumer trust to build a conceptual framework. It links four features of algorithmic pricing (real-time adaptation, personalization, individualized price differentiation, and limited explainability) to perceived price fairness, which in turn shapes consumer trust and acceptance or resistance. The paper argues that fairness is a strategic management problem, not only an ethical concern. Implications for pricing managers cover price explanations, responsible personalization, and governance, and empirical research directions are proposed.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: Background: Computer programmers face intensive cognitive demands, sustained concentration, tight deadlines, and extended working hours that may compromise occupational health. This study examined relationships among work-related burnout, insomnia, and psychological well-being among computer programmers in Lahore, Pakistan. Methods: A cross-sectional correlational study recruited 250 employed programmers, comprising 143 men and 107 women, aged 18–35 years. Data were collected between April and June 2024 through face-to-face questionnaires and Google Forms. Participants completed the Oldenburg Burnout Inventory, Bergen Insomnia Scale, and Psychological Well-Being Scale. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlations, simple linear regression, and independent-samples t tests in SPSS 23. Results: Burnout correlated positively with insomnia (r = .248, p < .01) and negatively with psychological well-being (r = −.159, p < .05). The insomnia–well-being correlation was nonsignificant (r = −.053, p = .401). Burnout explained 6.2% of insomnia variance and 2.5% of psychological well-being variance. Women reported significantly higher burnout (p = .005) and insomnia (p = .022) than men; their psychological well-being scores did not differ significantly (p = .108). Conclusion: Greater burnout was associated with more insomnia symptoms and modestly poorer psychological well-being among programmers. Occupational workload management and access to employee support deserve attention. Because this study was cross-sectional and relied on self-report measures, the findings should not be interpreted as evidence of causal relationships.

Abstract We saw that the parameters for a dental printing process have a significant influence on the quality of the dental printed part, such as the layer height, speed of printing, orientation of printing, exposure time, and some parameters related to the used resin. There are many tra ditional ways of choosing the parameters, which are mostly empirical, and consequently lead to errors of dimensions, flaws on surfaces, and high consumption of material; there is also high production time. An Artificial Intelligence (AI) supported optimization scheme is proposed here for the optimal selection of 3D printing parameters to increase the quality and the production efficiency of individual dental prostheses. The proposed approach consists of data acquisition, data collection/preprocessing, feature analysis, training of the machine learning models, and optimization of the parameters to find out correlation between the printing conditions and quality factors such as dimensional accuracy, surface roughness, manufacturing time and con sumption of the materials. Various performance metrics are employed to analyze the different machine learning models and then the best one is utilized to determine the optimum parameter. There are plans to minimize the trial and error methods and to select the parameters on a data driven basis.

Artificial Intelligence (AI) can simplify access to government welfare schemes by helping citizens identify schemes relevant to their needs and eligibility. This paper presents YojanaAI, an AI-based Government Scheme Recommendation System designed to support scheme discovery and eligibility assessment using user-specific information. The system aims to simplify the process of identifying suitable schemes based on relevant attributes such as age, income, occupation, and education. It provides a structured approach to accessing scheme details, eligibility requirements, and application information. The proposed system focuses on improving information accessibility and reducing the effort required to search multiple sources. Its effectiveness can be assessed through eligibility-matching accuracy, recommendation relevance, and usability testing. The paper outlines the proposed approach, potential applications, limitations, and future enhancements for developing accessible and citizen-centric digital public services.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: The article substantiates the feasibility of adaptive foreign language phonetics teaching, enhanced by artificial intelligence technologies, as an alternative to traditional standardized methods that fail to account for higher education students' individual articulatory features and lead to persistent phonetic errors. The study is interdisciplinary, combining the methodology of specialties A4 Secondary Education (A4.021 English Language and Literature), A5 Vocational Education (A5.39 Digital Technologies), and F7 Computer Engineering. The purpose of the study is to develop and justify a model of an adaptive learning platform for improving higher education students' phonetic skills through the integration of speech formant synthesis with machine learning algorithms. A formant synthesizer model based on parallel digital filters has been developed, generating reference vowel sounds by simulating the resonant frequencies of the vocal tract. An approach to personalizing learning is proposed based on a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) neural network, which analyzes a student's error history and dynamically adjusts formant parameters in real time. Technical validation of the model demonstrated high accuracy of formant frequency correction, with a root-mean-square error of 45 Hz for the first formant and 78 Hz for the second, enabling objective assessment of pronunciation quality and adaptation of exercise difficulty to the individual student's level. A pilot quasi-experimental verification of the platform involving experimental and control groups of higher education students confirmed its pedagogical potential for implementing differentiated learning principles based on objective acoustic data. The conclusions confirm the platform's prospects for modernizing linguistic education. Further research directions include expanding empirical validation on a larger sample and conducting perceptual evaluation of synthesized speech quality by native speakers to confirm its naturalness and suitability for learning purposes.
topics: Intelligent Tutoring Systems and Adaptive Learning

documents.abstract: Rapid digitalization in higher education, combined with the need for universities to operate under geographically distributed and relocated conditions, highlights a crucial shift from rigid hierarchical management to flexible, decentralized systems. This paper substantiates the architecture of decentralized university management models driven by multi-agent systems and large language models (LLMs), presenting its architectural justification and functional implementation within a higher education institution. The study details theoretical foundations of utilizing multi-agent systems, orchestration protocols, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), and vector databases to optimize university workflows under conditions of limited observability and distributed IT infrastructure. The methodology rests on a two-tier multi-agent architecture, where dynamic request routing is achieved through a hierarchical orchestration model using AgentSpec formal specifications, while action consistency is maintained by a central algorithmic coordinator. Findings indicate that deploying a standalone autonomous agent for each of the university’s 24 departments is inefficient due to risks of algorithmic conflicts, redundant queries to the vector knowledge base, increased LLM hallucination rates, and context window constraints. To address these limitations, a coordinated multi-agent architecture was implemented at Kherson State University. This framework consolidates operations into five core macro-agents—academic affairs, administrative management, knowledge management, educational quality assurance, and communications—managed by a Central Orchestrator routing queries, controlling access privileges, and synthesizing analytical outputs. The paper identifies key organizational and technological hurdles, focusing on maintaining high levels of trust, decision verification, and role-based access control during delegation. Finally, it outlines the roadmap for evolving this framework into a university digital twin capable of predictive modeling and automated process support. These findings offer practical value for higher education institutions deploying digital ecosystems under human resource, infrastructural, and security constraints.

Recent years have witnessed rapid advances in generative artificial intelligence (AI) models such as ChatGPT and Gemini, opening new prospects for supporting the educational process. This study aims to measure the effectiveness of generative AI models in improving university students' academic writing skills, using a quasi-experimental design with experimental and control groups (N = 60 second-year students of the Faculty of Education, randomly assigned to the two groups). The experimental group received a six-week training program that integrated generative AI as a writing assistant across brainstorming, drafting, language revision, and referencing, while the control group followed traditional instruction. An academic writing skills test and an observation checklist were used as instruments. The study hypothesizes statistically significant differences (α = 0.05) favoring the experimental group in thesis clarity, idea organization, linguistic accuracy, and academic referencing, alongside positive attitudes toward AI as a supportive tool rather than a substitute for thinking. In addition, an exploratory descriptive survey of 87 university students found that 93.1% had previously used generative AI tools for academic writing, 95.4% supported clear university policies governing their use, and 72.4% reported concern about over-reliance on them. The study recommends training faculty members to integrate generative AI tools into academic writing courses and establishing an ethical charter to govern their use.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Traditional circuit breakers provide protection against overcurrent and short-circuit conditions but have no inherent provision for remote supervision, demand awareness or intelligent load management. This paper introduces the design, implementation and experimental testing of a smart circuit breaker that combines independent electrical protection, hybrid Global System for Mobile communication (GSM)–Internet of Things (IoT) connectivity, and an energy optimization layer based on artificial intelligence (AI). An edge controller measures voltage, current, active power and energy in real time and publishes telemetry through a Message Queuing Telemetry Transport (MQTT) link or, when Internet connectivity is lost, through the GSM short-message service (SMS). A hybrid Long Short-Term Memory–Extreme Gradient Boosting (LSTM–XGBoost) model forecasts short-term demand, and a weighted objective function schedules deferrable loads to minimize electricity cost and peak demand while satisfying circuit-capacity and user-priority constraints. Software and communication functions never substitute for hardware protection; a certified miniature circuit breaker (MCB) remains the primary fault-interruption device. the prototype measured the electrical quantities with a maximum loaded-condition deviation of 0.76% from the calibrated reference values; the forecaster achieved an RMSE of 0.083 kW and a coefficient of determination (R²) of 0.9899; and the hybrid channel maintained a 97.1% command-success rate during controlled Internet-outage trials, whereas the IoT-only channel recorded 0%. Compared with conventional operation, the AI-driven strategy reduced peak demand by 39.6% and electricity cost by 8.0%, whereas total energy consumption decreased by only 3.0%, indicating that its main advantage is peak-demand reduction rather than energy reduction. These findings indicate the feasibility of a deployable device that combines protection, resilient communication and predictive energy management.

The purpose of this article was to 1) develop problem-based learning (PBL) activities integrated with gamification, and 2) compare Grade 9 students’ mathematics learning achievement before and after learning through the developed activities. The participants were 30 Grade 9 students from Ban Kanit PeeRuangkhao, Selected randomly from a population normally distributed. The research instruments included (1) lesson plans based on PBL integrated with gamification, (2) an activity suitablility evaluation form and (3) a trigonometry achievement test. The data were analyzed using percentage, mean, standard deviation and a dependent-sample t-test. The findings revealed that 1) the developed learning activities were highly appropriate, characterized by problem-solving scenarios and gamified motivational element, 2) students’ post-test scores were significantly higher than their pre-test scores at the .01 level and 3) students demonstrated greater enthusiasm and engagement in learning. The study indicates that integrating PBL and gamification effectively enhances students’ mathematics learning achievement and fosters intrinsic motivation toward active learning.

In the 2021 Olympics, high jumpers Barshim and Tamberi and in the 2023 World Athletics Championships pole vaulters Moon and Kennedy refused tiebreak procedures (the jump-off) after clearing the same height. The athletes thus shared gold medals. Deliberate jump-off refusals can challenge the conventional Olympic motto (faster, higher, stronger), highlight the significance of ties as meaningful resolutions without privileging participation over victory, and foreground mutualism over self-distinguishing gain. By agreeing to stop together, athletes redefine sporting excellence as shared and as divorced from more-than-human performance; they also reject the imposition to prioritize fan entertainment. Moreover, the acknowledgement of mutual limits underscores a consideration of measure and ultimately of virtue as moderation.

"Major industrial accidents constitute one of the most critical risk areas of modern industrial societies due to their high destructive effects despite their low probabilities of occurrence. Cases throughout history prove that these events arise not only from technical failures, but also from organizational weaknesses, systemic deficiencies, human factors, and inadequately designed safety systems. Root cause analyses reveal that the underlying causes of accidents are the insufficient analysis of reaction kinetics, the failure to correctly evaluate the accident chain developing after the loss of control, and, most importantly, the failure to keep risk analyses up to date. This situation proves that process safety should not be limited only to engineering design; it makes a holistic approach encompassing operational discipline, human factors, and organizational learning capacity necessary. The dioxin release that occurred in the town of Seveso, Italy, as a result of the uncontrolled shutdown of a reactor and the failure to correctly evaluate the by-products that could be released, fundamentally changed the European perspective on industrial safety and paved the way for the issuance of the first Seveso Directive. The Seveso Directives established within the European Union and the Regulation on the Prevention of Major Industrial Accidents and Mitigation of Their Effects (BEKRA Regulation), which entered into force in our country in line with these directives, constitute the fundamental legal and technical infrastructure for the prevention of accidents and minimization of their damages within the scope of technological disaster management. The Bhopal tragedy, which occurred despite the first directive being in force, and the Baia Mare accident, which resulted in environmental damage crossing national borders, became milestones in industrial safety and enabled the principle of “preventability of accidents” to be replaced by a more comprehensive understanding of “risk management.” In this process, critical requirements such as the domino effect, land-use planning, and informing the public were introduced into the directives. Lessons learned from experienced industrial accidents reveal that the “prescriptive” approach alone is not sufficient in the integration of safety management systems into processes. Current requirements make it necessary to adopt a “performance-based” approach that goes beyond the set of rules. Although significant progress has been made in our country in terms of regulatory compliance, there are still areas for improvement regarding process safety culture, organizational learning processes, and the internalization of advanced risk analysis techniques. For effective accident risk management, compliance with only regulatory parameters should not be considered sufficient; a performance-based, holistic, and sustainable process safety strategy should be ensured to permeate all operational processes. It is of critical importance that future studies strengthen interdisciplinary approaches and focus particularly on safety culture and organizational learning processes."

Across modern literary history, children have served as powerful symbolic figures through which societies negotiate core social values. Yet despite their prominence in canonical criticism, we lack a systematic account of how often children appear in novels, how they are valued, and what kinds of agency they are afforded over time. To address this gap, I conduct a large-scale computational analysis of 9,544 English-language novels published between 1800 and 2000. This study provides the first large-scale extraction of child characters from the modern novel, combining classical natural language processing with large language models to measure their visibility, emotional valuation, narrative agency, and independence from kinship structures. Contrary to dominant histories of childhood, children and adolescents become progressively less visible in the novel over time, a decline driven by the erosion of the adolescent girl in particular. Children maintain a more positive emotional valence than adults even as their agency lags behind adult peers, suggesting a broader portrait of children as sentimentally valued, yet structurally constrained social actors.

The rapid development of cloud technology, big data, and artificial intelligence has changed the way data pipelines are managed in today’s world. Conventional data pipeline management systems depend on rule-based automation and manual intervention making them less effective in managing dynamic workloads, detecting anomalies, recovering from faults, and optimizing resources. The recent advances in Agentic Artificial Intelligence, LLMs, reinforcement learning, and multi-agent systems have given rise to the autonomous systems that can perform monitoring, diagnosis, recovery, and optimization on their own. This review studies the state-of-the-art AI information pipeline management processes, intelligent work flow orchestration, autonomous decision making, and self-healing systems. The paper reviews the existing methodologies, including ETL automation, metadata-based data ingestion, optimization through reinforcement learning, and agent-based orchestration systems, and presents their advantages, limitations, and potential fields of application. Moreover, the review identifies main research problems faced by researchers and developers including explainability, interoperability, scalability, security, and adaptation in heterogeneous cloud environments.

The shift from Industry 4.0 to Industry 5.0 marks a profound paradigm evolution in strategic human resource management (HRM), transitioning from pure technological automation to human-centric socio-technical synergy, sustainability, and organizational resilience. This critical review synthesizes peer-reviewed literature published between 2021 and 2026 to evaluate the influence of digital HR transformation—encompassing artificial intelligence, predictive people analytics, cloud-based HRIS, and collaborative robotics (cobots)—on multi-dimensional employee engagement (vigor, dedication, and absorption). Guided by the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA 2020) framework, 16 benchmark empirical and conceptual studies were systematically selected and categorized. The synthesis reveals that while digital HR transformation significantly drives operational efficiency, its direct impact on employee engagement is mediated by digital fluency, perceived organizational support, and psychological safety. Furthermore, algorithmic transparency and responsible data governance serve as critical moderators that mitigate techno-stress, privacy anxieties, and algorithmic burnout. The paper delivers an integrative socio-technical framework for Industry 5.0, offering strategic guidance for organizational leaders seeking to align cutting-edge HR technologies with human well-being and sustainable performance.

In contemporary organizational research, the imperative to balance economic productivity with human sustainability has elevated Sustainable Human Resource Management (Sustainable HRM) into a core strategic framework. This critical review systematically evaluates 16 benchmark empirical and conceptual studies published between 2021 and 2026 to investigate how Sustainable HRM practices influence tri-dimensional employee well-being (physical, psychological, and social) and long-term organizational performance. Adhering to PRISMA 2020 systematic review protocols, this study synthesizes structural equation modelling (SEM) findings, panel econometrics, and qualitative case studies across diverse industrial and geographical settings. The synthesis reveals that while traditional HRM prioritizes short-term transactional output, Sustainable HRM embeds ergonomic work design, psychological safety, work-life boundary protection, and green employee voice, yielding a significant positive effect on psychological capital (β = 0.44, p < .001) and work-family enrichment (β = 0.41, p < .001). Meta-analyzed structural models demonstrate that physical and psychological well-being fully mediate the relationship between sustainable work practices and employee job performance (β = 0.38, p < .001), while drastically reducing turnover intentions. However, critical gaps persist regarding paradoxical workload pressures under green mandates and regional implementation disparities. This paper presents a multi-level governance framework providing actionable pathways for HR leaders to operationalize sustainable well-being.

Systematized Nomenclature of Medicine – Clinical Terms (SNOMED CT) enables semantically interoperable health data, but implementation in Thailand is hindered by language and workflow challenges. We evaluated whether large language models (LLMs) can automate SNOMED CT concept extraction from Thai clinical documents. The objectives of this study are to develop a proof-of-concept framework for automated clinical named entity recognition and SNOMED CT concept linking from Thai medical documents, and to compare the performance and resource requirements of closed-source and open-source LLMs on a human-annotated dataset. The dataset was manually annotated from 220 Thai medical documents (6,390 entities) from three outpatient departments. Our retrieval-augmented framework was evaluated using four LLMs (Gemini 2.5 Pro, GPT-4.1, Qwen 3, and MedGemma) as experimental based models which were comparatively analyzed for entity recognition using precision, recall, F1 score and concept linking using character-level metric, Intersection over Union (IoU), as well as resource consumptions. For entity recognition, Gemini achieved the highest performance (loose F1 83.31%). For SNOMED CT concept extraction ranked most similar (Top-1) by encoder models for retrieval and re-ranking, IoU scores were 39.42% (Gemini), 34.44% (GPT), 29.86% (MedGemma), and 28.62% (Qwen). Average processing time for end-to-end extraction was 5–6 minutes per document for Gemini and GPT, with cost estimates in United states dollars (USD) of USD 0.035 and USD 0.019 per document, respectively; local open-source inference required up to 10 minutes per document. This study established a proof-of-concept framework for automated clinical entity recognition and SNOMED CT concept linking from Thai medical documents, demonstrating practical LLM performance with trade-offs between accuracy, cost, and efficiency across closed-source and open-source models.

Voxel-level kinetic modeling in total-body dynamic positron emission tomography (TB-PET) enables precise physiological quantification but complicates parameter uncertainty estimation. While generative consistency models (CMs) can rapidly estimate Bayesian posterior distributions, they are constrained by type of tracers, kinetic models, and protocols. Training them from scratch whenever a new tracer, model or protocol is used can be computationally intensive. To address this, we introduce LoRACM, a parameter-efficient framework utilizing low-rank adaptation (LoRA) to transfer a pretrained foundation CM to novel TB-PET scenarios. We evaluated three adaptation scenarios using simulated and human data: scanner and protocol transfer for FDG two-tissue compartment modeling; FP-CIT simplified reference tissue modeling; and high-temporal-resolution FDG blood flow imaging via the adiabatic approximation to tissue homogeneity model. Each adaptation was trained in less than 3 hours on a single NVIDIA A100 GPU using 50,000 simulated pairs. In simulations, LoRACM showed strong agreement with results from Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC, which we use as reference posterior distributions), yielding median Kullback-Leibler divergences of 0.05-0.11 and median absolute percentage errors below 1.2% for each kinetic parameter of interest. In human data, LoRACM generated total-body K_i maps comparable to the ones made by non-negative nonlinear least squares (NNLS) fitting and a consistency model trained from scratch. Striatal dopamine binding potential estimates predicted by LoRACM correlated with NNLS estimates (r = 0.968-0.988). LoRACM produced total-body blood flow imaging with FDG matching the one made by NNLS. These underscore the potential of adapting a pretrained CM with LoRA for fast and reliable posterior parameter inference for kinetic models across distinct TB-PET applications.

As generative artificial intelligence (GAI) reshapes business education, instructors must simultaneously safeguard academic integrity and develop students’ AI literacy for an increasingly AI-driven workplace. This study developed the GAI Learning Framework (GLF), a replicable, step-by-step experiential learning approach for case-based projects in undergraduate business courses, illustrated through an operations management (OM) application. Rather than enabling passive cognitive offloading, the GLF promotes active learning by requiring students to craft context-rich prompts grounded in course materials, systematically compare outputs across multiple GAI platforms (e.g., ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini), and critically evaluate discrepancies against independently verified sources. The framework was implemented across two sections of an undergraduate OM course and evaluated using a student survey that combined Likert-scale items with open-ended reflections (n = 50). All three constructs exceeded the scale midpoint, with pooled means ranging from 3.93 (Constructive Alignment) to 4.08 (Cognitive Load/Scaffolding). Qualitative student reflections further indicated that students perceived the framework as fostering active learning, AI platform literacy, and professional communication skills. This study offers educators a practical, classroom-tested framework for integrating GAI tools into case-based projects in business courses while preserving analytical rigor and promoting experiential learning. Supplemental Material: The online appendices are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/ited.2026.0224 .

Landslides are among the most destructive natural hazards in mountainous regions, yet susceptibility mapping in data-scarce areas remains challenging. This study proposes a reproducible Geospatial Artificial Intelligence (GeoAI) framework that integrates Google Earth Engine (GEE), ensemble machine learning, and explainable AI (XAI) for landslide susceptibility mapping in central Nepal. Using a balanced dataset of 9,479 observations from 4,743 landslide and 4,736 non-landslide locations, extracted seven conditioning factors: topographic (elevation, slope, aspect), climatic (rainfall), ecological (NDVI, land cover), and anthropogenic (population density) within the GEE cloud computing environment. Random Forest (RF) and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) models using stratified train-test splitting and 10-fold cross-validation. Both models showed strong predictive performance, with XGBoost achieving superior results (Accuracy: 88.3%, ROC-AUC: 0.952) compared to RF (Accuracy: 87.9%, ROC-AUC: 0.945). SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) identified slope as the most influential predictor associated with model predictions followed by rainfall (16%) and elevation (15%), while lower NDVI values consistently correlated with higher susceptibility. The susceptibility map identified high-risk zones concentrated in Sindhupalchok, Dolakha, Dhading, Rasuwa, Gorkha, and Nuwakot districts. This framework reveals that freely available satellite data, cloud computing, and explainable machine learning can be effectively integrated for susceptibility mapping and community resilience initiatives.

The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) with geospatial analysis, commonly referred to as GeoAI, provides new opportunities for renewable-energy planning and site-suitability assessment. However, limited attention has been given to integrating Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis (MCDA) with machine learning (ML) for offshore wind farm suitability assessment. This study proposes a GeoAI framework to predict offshore wind farm suitability using ensemble machine-learning techniques. A pooled technology-aware ML model was developed using nine predictors, including a turbine type to account for fixed-bottom and floating technologies. Gradient Boosting, XGBoost, LightGBM, Random Forest, Decision Tree, and Logistic Regression were evaluated, with a majority-class classifier included as a baseline. Model development and hyperparameter optimization were conducted using five-fold stratified group cross-validation based on geographic blocks, with weighted F1-score used as the primary model-selection metric. Gradient Boosting achieved the best model, with a weighted F1-score of 0.8077, followed closely by XGBoost (0.8031), and was therefore selected for final evaluation. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis further revealed that wind power density, wind speed, and water depth were the most influential factors governing offshore wind farm suitability predictions.

Background Hospitals routinely collect wide-ranging data related to quality, efficiency, and clinical practice. As part of these efforts, patient safety event data are collected, compiled, and analyzed to drive process improvement. Methods We present a novel adaptation and application of the Department of Defense Human Factors Analysis and Classification System (HFACS) as a heuristic tool to improve the conduct of root cause analysis (RCA) sessions that follow serious patient safety events. To assess individual knowledge improvement after reviewing the heuristic tool, a 1-page summary (including a graphical image of the tool) was developed and provided to a convenience sample of staff in our facility (N = 48). Participants were asked to read over the information and then answer a 5-question survey about their knowledge of the RCA process. A Likert scale was used to assess participants’ level of knowledge prior to, and following, their exposure to the 1-page summary. Results Mean Likert scores increased from 2.83 to 3.42 (Δ = +0.59), reflecting improved self-reported participant perception of knowledge gained around RCA principles (paired t-test: t(47) = 4.10, P < .001) with a medium effect size (Cohen’s d = 0.59). Conclusion The results from this pilot study suggest that this heuristic tool may improve knowledge of RCA concepts among clinical staff. At higher levels of an organization, improved accuracy and precision of locally entered data would also improve centralized human factor data analysis to inform decision-making.

Seed implant brachytherapy (SIBT) is an effective cancer treatment modality; however, clinical planning often relies on manual adjustment of objective function weights, leading to inefficiencies and suboptimal results. This study proposes an adaptive weight optimization framework for SIBT planning, driven by large language models (LLMs). A locally deployed DeepSeek-R1 LLM is integrated with an automatic planning algorithm in an iterative loop. Starting with fixed weights, the LLM evaluates plan quality and recommends new weights in the next iteration. This process continues until convergence criteria are met, after which the LLM conducts a comprehensive evaluation to identify the optimal plan. A clinical knowledge base, constructed and queried via retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), enhances the model's domain-specific reasoning. The proposed method was retrospectively validated on 23 patient cases who underwent head-and-neck SIBT, showing that the LLM-assisted approach maintained clinical target volume (CTV) coverage and reduced excessive target dose relative to fixed-weight planning; in the eight patients with available organs at risk (OARs) contours, OAR dose metrics showed favorable numerical trends. The study demonstrates the potential of LLMs as assistive tools for SIBT planning under clinician supervision.

documents.abstract: Automated crack segmentation is a key component of vision-based structural health monitoring for civil infrastructure. However, many deep learning approaches remain computationally demanding for embedded edge devices and exhibit limited generalisation across diverse materials and imaging conditions. This paper presents a lightweight deep learning architecture designed to balance segmentation accuracy, computational efficiency, and cross-domain robustness. The artificial intelligence contribution is an efficient encoder–decoder integrating depthwise separable convolutions, lightweight multi-scale context aggregation, and channel attention. The proposed approach targets crack continuity through a unified design for thin-structure segmentation under strict computational constraints. The engineering contribution is a practical inspection method for structural health monitoring systems with limited memory, latency, and power budgets. Experiments on a joint dataset comprising 30,017 crack images collected from 20 heterogeneous datasets demonstrate competitive performance across diverse conditions. The proposed Lightweight Attention Channel-Enhanced Crack Segmentation (LACE-Crack) architecture achieves a higher harmonic mean of precision and recall (F1 score) (0.569 vs. 0.566), precision (0.751 vs. 0.732), mean intersection over union (0.694 vs. 0.693), optimal image scale (0.489 vs. 0.480), and optimal dataset scale (0.425 vs. 0.411) than the comparison architecture, with comparable recall (0.459 vs. 0.462). It also requires approximately 43% fewer parameters and 64% fewer floating-point operations. These results demonstrate a strong balance between crack segmentation performance and computational efficiency, supporting the practical use of lightweight artificial intelligence for infrastructure inspection under deployment constraints.
topics: Industrial Vision Systems and Defect Detection

documents.abstract: This scoping review aimed to examine the methodological characteristics and performance of artificial intelligence (AI)-based speech intelligibility assessment in individuals with acquired motor speech disorders. It also evaluated the clinical applicability of AI-based assessment by reviewing the relationship between AI-based assessments and human perceptual ratings. Four international databases (PubMed, IEEE Xplore, Web of Science, and ScienceDirect) and three Korean databases (KISS, DBPIA, and RISS) were searched up to March 2026. Fifteen studies were selected after applying predefined exclusion criteria. The selected studies were classified and synthesized descriptively without risk-of-bias assessment. 1) Reading tasks were the most frequently used speech task across the 15 included studies, regardless of the data collection method. 2) A wide range of automatic speech recognition systems (e.g., Google Cloud ASR API; Google LLC, Mountain View, CA, USA) and machine learning and deep learning models (e.g., bidirectional long-short term memory, convolutional neural networks, support vector machines, and linear regression) were used, with no single approach predominating. 3) Many studies reported strong correlations or high levels of agreement between AI-based assessments and human perceptual ratings, whereas some reported weak correlations or nonlinear relationships. The included studies generally reported positive associations between AI-based and perceptual intelligibility measures, although the performance metrics and models varied considerably across studies. Therefore, the findings should be interpreted with caution in clinical applications.

Systematic comparisons of the classic airfoil literature with modern codes have been limited less by physics than by the labour of extracting data from scanned charts. This study shows that optical character recognition and an AI agent, working under the author’s direction, can automate this chain: source retrieval, chart calibration, visual data reading, simulation campaigns, quality control and documentation. With this workflow, all 112 section charts of NACA Report 824 and three planform figures of Hoerner’s Fluid-Dynamic Lift were recomputed with XFOIL, MSES and AVL in about 7.5 hours of elapsed time. Lift-curve slopes agree to a median +2.2 % (XFOIL), and the overprediction grows with thickness. Zero-lift angles are too negative in proportion to camber in both codes; transition modelling and tunnel-wall corrections were ruled out as causes. Drag is underpredicted by about 15 % at all Reynolds numbers. The offset vanishes for Ncrit ≈ 5, an effective parameter for surface imperfections or the shared boundary-layer model. Maximum lift is overpredicted, most for thin sections. AVL reproduces Hoerner’s planform data within a few per cent where the flow is attached and the edges are sharp. Automated checks found errors in the source, the codes and the agent’s own work; human verification remains essential.

In the modern era, using the technology of image processing, people are being facilitated in many sectors. Therefore, we have decided to do research on cow recognition using the methods of image processing. Because cows are pretty essential for human beings, and people from the entire world are being facilitated by cows. Because of that reason, many technologies have been invented till now for the cow. Here we have presented an approach to identify the cow. Like the fingerprint of a human, the cow muzzle is also unique. Due to this reason, we can recognize the cow based on the muzzle. To recognize muzzles, we have used Yolo and the Structural Similarity Index (SSI). Image processing is a sector of Artificial Intelligence and data is quite important to train models. Moreover, to train a model for image processing, it is needed to manage a high-configuration computer. But there are many regions in the world where people hardly get such powerful machines. To mitigate this issue, we have introduced a unique method where we do not need a large amount of data for the image processing task. To eliminate the necessity of collecting a huge amount of data, we included a self- enhancing feature, which helps the model to predict accurately and also helps to improve performance by increasing the amount of data. However, without a large amount of data, it will be possible to predict appropriately because of the presence of self-enhancing features. This certain program helps the model to improve its capability for delivering faster responses. LLM is responsible to add the self-enhancing feature. On the other hand, to find out the most suitable Yolo model for our research, we have trained data with three different versions of Yolo: Yolo v7, v8, and v9. We evaluated the performances of these three versions in terms of Precision, Recall, mAP50, and mAP50-95 and found Yolo v9 to be the best among them. It excels with a precision of 0.391, a recall of 0.916, a mAP50 of 0.559, and a mAP50-95 of 0.307.

Credit scoring is fundamental in enabling institutions to distinguish between creditworthy and high-risk borrowers. Thus, robust credit scoring models are essential for effective financial risk management. Artificial intelligence and machine learning have significantly improved the precision of credit decision support systems, however, these models often operate as black boxes, concealing the underlying logic of credit denials or approvals. To address this challenge and meet the demand for financial transparency, explainable AI (XAI) has emerged as a crucial mechanism for generating decisions that are interpretable to both financial institutions and clients. This paper researched contemporary decision support systems (DSS) used in credit risk assessment and proposes a modular, plug-and-play framework with integrated explainability. Six requirements were derived for a robust system design based on a review of existing XAI frameworks. The framework consists of five interconnected components such as data ingestion layer, feature processing module, a supervised predictive model, an explanation layer, and a decision endpoint. Existing studies often focus on individual predictive models or explanation methods, leaving their integration and component interchangeability unspecified. The proposed framework addresses this gap through explicit interfaces that allow predictive models and explanation methods to be replaced independently. The system will operate with both traditional credit data, alternative data, or both. Thus, feature processing is incorporated to distinguish the importance and relevance of the data to credit assessment decisions. Any irrelevant redundant data is not be considered by the model. The contribution of a study is a reusable architectural specification. The proposed XAI framework is designed to serve as a universal template for researchers and financial institutions developing transparent, effective credit scoring systems.

Patients often arrive at brief, time-constrained clinical visits unsure of what to expect or ask, and millions of adults now turn to general-purpose AI chatbots to prepare beforehand. Yet whether conversational AI improves visit readiness remains unclear. We designed a large language model (LLM)-based visit preparation agent to guide patients before an appointment by gathering clinical context, setting visit expectations, providing relevant health information, building a prioritized list of questions for their clinician, and generating a summary. In a prospective consented randomized study in the Google Health app, 802 U.S. adults held 866 health-related conversations with the visit preparation agent (standard or concise variant) or a minimally prompted control chatbot built on the same LLM. The visit preparation agent significantly outperformed the control across blinded clinician evaluations and patient self-reports. In clinician reviews of completed sessions (n = 272), the agent achieved a 16.6% higher rate of comprehensive preparation (67.2% vs. 50.6%; P < 0.05) and an 8.5% higher rate of alignment with patients' health context (98.9% vs. 90.4%; P < 0.01), while maintaining high medical safety and appropriateness across all study arms. Patient post-surveys (n = 460) showed 16.8% higher visit preparedness (73.8% vs. 57.0%; P < 0.01), 14.3% higher confidence in knowing what to ask (81.4% vs. 67.1%; P < 0.01), and 12.0% higher overall satisfaction (74.0% vs. 62.0%; P < 0.05). Clinician and participant metrics were not significantly correlated, indicating that expert review and patient self-assessment capture complementary dimensions of patient-facing AI. These findings suggest that LLM chatbots can safely help patients prepare for clinical visits, with greater benefit when following a structured workflow, and motivate future studies on in-visit communication and clinical outcomes.
